response:
The solution using a hash set is the most efficient one. Here's the Python code for it:
```python
def findPair(arr, x):
    num_set = set()
    for num in arr:
        complement = x - num
        if complement in num_set:
            return True
        num_set.add(num)
    return False

arr = [5, 20, 3, 2, 50, 80]
x = 78
if findPair(arr, x):
    print("true")
else:
    print("false")
```
This code creates a set `num_set` to store the numbers it has seen so far. For each number in the array, it checks if its complement (`x - num`) is already in the set. If it is, it returns True immediately. Otherwise, it adds the current number to the set. At the end of the loop, it returns False if no pair was found.

This solution has a time complexity of O(n), where n is the length of the array, because each insertion and lookup operation in the set takes constant time on average.
